questions.q: What does a network-based IDS (NIDS) like Snort or Suricata typically monitor?
options: A copy of traffic crossing a network segment, usually via a SPAN or mirror port
Only encrypted traffic that other tools can't see
Nothing — NIDS tools are purely theoretical
Only the file integrity of a single host
questions.explain: A NIDS watches a mirrored copy of traffic crossing a network segment, the same deployment model used by an IDS in Lesson 5.

questions.q: What can a NIDS see that a single HIDS agent cannot?
options: Cross-host patterns, like one machine scanning many others across the network
Nothing — a NIDS has no visibility a HIDS lacks
A process tree running entirely on one machine
A local file that was modified on one specific host
questions.explain: Because a NIDS sees traffic from every host on a segment, it can spot network-wide patterns a single host's HIDS agent never would.

questions.q: What does a host-based IDS (HIDS) like OSSEC watch?
options: Nothing on the host itself — only network traffic destined for it
Only traffic matching a signature database, never host-local activity
Traffic crossing every segment of the entire network
That one system's own logs, file integrity, and process activity, from an agent installed on it
questions.explain: A HIDS runs as an agent on one system and watches that system's logs, file integrity, and processes from the inside.

questions.q: What is a key blind spot of a HIDS compared to a NIDS?
options: A HIDS only sees the one system it's installed on and has no network-wide visibility
A HIDS has no blind spots at all
A HIDS requires a SPAN port to function
A HIDS can never detect any local file changes
questions.explain: A HIDS agent is scoped to a single host, so it has zero visibility into anything happening elsewhere on the network.

questions.q: Why do SOCs typically deploy both NIDS and HIDS rather than relying on just one?
options: Each one covers blind spots the other structurally cannot see, giving defense in depth
Running both has no additional benefit over running just one
NIDS and HIDS are actually the same technology under different names
Regulations require exactly two IDS tools regardless of type
questions.explain: A NIDS catches network-wide patterns while a HIDS catches host-local activity, so together they cover each other's gaps.
